scope: YM C4basic trig decisions,proof methods,bounded equations,inverse values and source investigations. Five insights cover ten M1T6 demands; shared progression facets already grouped separately.

families.title: Sketch a basic trig curve and its reflected partner
families.learner_decisions: Plot the actual restricted basic curve, reflect its ordinates and describe the reflection.
families.givens_and_unknowns: sin/cos/tan and their negatives; unknown paired sketches and transformation.
families.constraints: Retain the actual degree/radian unit, strict/closed endpoints and original natural domain. Tangent/reciprocal poles remain excluded after algebra. Exact and decimal answers are distinct instructions. Preserve all registered print/key defects.
families.representation_and_response: Function formula to labelled shared sketches and explanation.
families.scaffolding_and_connected_parts: Both sketches and the stated reflection are required; asymptotes are not finite plotted points.
families.alternative_methods: Key-point/symmetry sketches or exact transformed coordinates.
families.units_and_precision: Preserve the literal angular unit, original interval endpoints, exact-form or decimal instruction and physical dimensions. Intermediate approximations must not change the final rounding or admissibility.
families.answer_form: Correct restricted shapes, intercepts, asymptotes and reflection.
families.difficulty_progression: YM10 uses radian tangent; Try10 switches function and degree/radian interval.
families.distinction_basis: A paired transformation explanation differs from a single formula sketch.

insights.title: Basic and transformed trig graphs
insights.teaching_comparison: YM uses base-function plotting investigations, separates a/b/c effects, then moves from features to sketches and supplied-graph deductions. GoldieC3 begins at reciprocal graphs/R-form applications and assumes these foundations. The source investigations retain all rows rather than counting each parameter row as a new type.
insights.examination_comparison: The part-to-demand examination matrix distinguishes supplied-graph reading from learner sketching. Given point values for a sinusoid do not supply graph-reading evidence. YM12(c) changes function and its printed solution wrongly repeats the old curve; this is not an allowable marker alternative.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: E06 supplies basic trig graphs;C06/A06 include transformed amplitude/period/sketch/interpretation. Harder source chains add named coordinates, inequalities, a suitable chosen line or multiple functions. Keep those branches within the actual small-integer/simple-fraction scope.
insights.pitfalls: Tangent has no amplitude; the visible window need not contain a full cycle or a global extremum. Try15Q1 and Exercise4.2Q5 have wrong printed curve labels. Simultaneous sign changes can leave a recovered formula unchanged unless signs are restricted.
insights.gaps_and_representations: YM has unusually broad technology/table practice; Goldie offers complementary reciprocal/R-form visual work. These investigations support explanations but are not all observed exam structures. Required sketch responses stay distinct from worked-solution pictures.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose graph-reading, feature-reading, sketch and graph-deduction branches with exact windows, units, poles and feature rubrics. Separate source-given parameters from inferred ones and preserve parameter nonuniqueness where warranted.

insights.title: Exact special angles and connected geometry
insights.teaching_comparison: YM derives45 and30/60 values from exact triangles, then uses related angles, ratio arithmetic and connected geometry. Goldie3A begins with reciprocal special values and3B compounds them into75/15degree values. A derived non-special compound angle is not the same reasoning as a memorised basic value.
insights.examination_comparison: 8227 direct special-value links include connected questions; using a special value incidentally is a component link. Source wording without a calculator may require exact working rather than a decimal angle substituted back.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: C06 explicitly names exact special/related angles. The easiest branch recalls/evaluates a ratio; harder diagrams require choosing the correct triangle and connecting an inverse angle relation. That does not add general unsupported geometry.
insights.pitfalls: Try18Q1(c) key answersCD rather thanBC. Try28 ratios need positive radius and signed coordinates. A requested squared ratio does not require the same sign selection as an unsquared one.
insights.gaps_and_representations: YM has more basic diagram scaffolding; Goldie adds reciprocal/compound variety. Keep each right-angle, midpoint and collinearity fact explicit and consistent with the generated diagram.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose exact-ratio, signed-related-angle and connected-geometry branches. Preserve no-calculator instructions and accept valid exact alternatives independently of the printed key.

insights.title: Principal inverse values and restricted inverse functions
insights.teaching_comparison: YM states principal ranges, gives exact/calculator illustrations, then solves unknown-input inverse equations and restricted inverse-function/graph chains. GoldieC11Activity8 supplies a retained principal-arctangent/range exercise amid otherwise excluded complex-number material.
insights.examination_comparison: The defective2023P1Q9 is held; it does not establish a valid original principal-value exemplar. This demand remains syllabus-derived with comparable Cambridge evidence as separately recorded. Do not use an inverse-function problem as automatic evidence for every inverse-value decision.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: E06 explicitly includes principal inverse notation. The hard source branches add polynomial input and branch-restricted inverse graphs while retaining the same finite principal ranges.
insights.pitfalls: Try53 asks degrees but prints radians. Source principal-range reminders have label/endpoint defects. atan never attains plus/minuspi/2. Squaring an input equation can add invalid candidates.
insights.gaps_and_representations: YM offers coherent progression; Goldie gives a targeted retained facet. Inverse graph sketches need original restriction and reflected endpoints, not just a symbolic inverse formula.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose single-value, unknown-input and restricted-function branches. Validate every input/range and original equation; keep the held original hidden and source corrections internal.

insights.title: Basic-identity proof structures
insights.teaching_comparison: YM explicitly distinguishes expansion/grouping, fractional aggregation, conjugates and both-side/common-expression methods. Goldie starts reciprocal Pythagorean identities and builds compound/double identities. A numerical check is useful for an error, not a proof of an identity.
insights.examination_comparison: Proof and hence-solve are separate assessed responses. The held2023P1Q1(b) source defect requiresa nonzero; its unqualified form is not a valid proof exemplar. Textbook proof text is internal evidence rather than official award wording.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: C06/A06 name proving with basic identities. The hard end changes the proof route and domain control, not merely the number of terms. Do not assume Bloom from the word prove.
insights.pitfalls: Cancellation may narrow or remove original domain points; a simpler right-hand side cannot extend an original quotient identity. Squared or conjugate routes need nonzero conditions and must not assume the target.
insights.gaps_and_representations: YM provides extensive proof-route practice; Goldie stresses checking versus proving. Similar-looking final expressions can need different evidence and should remain method branches.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose explicit proof-route alternatives and common-domain ledgers, plus a real dependency when a later equation must use the identity. Criteria must credit the learner argument, not a memorised target line.

insights.title: Transform equations and enumerate complete bounded solutions
insights.teaching_comparison: YM progresses from one ratio through squared values, negative windows, scaled/shifted arguments, zero factors, quadratics and proof/hence chains. Goldie3B/3C adds compound/double-angle reductions; the full interval and original domain still decide which roots survive.
insights.examination_comparison: Examination evidence distinguishes transforming a stated equation from its full finite solution set. LIMIT02 excludes general solutions. Textbook Exercise4.2Q3 lacks a stated interval/unit; its silently assumed one-cycle key is not a sound fresh instance.
insights.difficulty_and_grade_bounds: C06/A06 include small-integer/simple-fraction multiples and equations easily reducible to basic forms. Increase difficulty by changing the admissible branches, argument window or required reduction, not by inventing an unbounded general-solution requirement.
insights.pitfalls: Cancellingcos/sin loses valid zeros; taking one square-root sign loses ratio branches. Conversely clearing original poles can add false roots. Repeated polynomial roots and inclusive endpoints must be deduplicated correctly.
insights.gaps_and_representations: YM gives more foundation/windows; Goldie enriches identity-choice and contextual compound forms. Graph counting and analytic root listing remain different response demands; no sampled exam absence removes a syllabus-required demand.
insights.implications_for_step3: Propose independent original-equation and interval checks, branch-complete root lists, explicit hence edges and correct precision/angle modes. Keep no-solution branches valid and distinguish an ambiguous original from an author-corrected adaptation.
